test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements.

Statements:

Some cars are bikes.

All bikes are trucks.

Conclusions:

(I) Some trucks are cars.

(II) All trucks are cars.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c747ed5a8e5c8c65ff9539b6e756d2a545e170b3442433c96714c9ecfe4e4f1.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some trucks are cars → Follow (As some cars are bikes and all bikes are trucks. As whole bikes comes in trucks and has some part common with cars, therefore it is true)

(II) All trucks are cars→ Does not follow (As some cars are bikes and all bikes are trucks. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (I) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2"
